stone.notes: Basic full block. Solid grey building stone.

stone_bricks.notes: Bedrock id is stone_bricks (plural). Variants via separate ids (mossy/cracked/chiseled) in modern Bedrock, not a state.

states.pillar_axis: x | y | z (rotated pillar-style block, like logs)

deepslate.notes: Dark deep-underground stone. Has pillar_axis like a log.

grass_block.notes: Bedrock id is grass_block (not just 'grass', which is the plant/short_grass).

oak_planks.notes: Oak wood planks. Wood-type variants are separate ids in modern Bedrock (spruce_planks etc).

states.pillar_axis: x | y | z (orientation of the log/pillar)

oak_log.notes: pillar_axis controls log orientation. y is upright.

states.weirdo_direction: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 (the facing of the stairs - Bedrock's quirky name for stair direction)

oak_stairs.notes: Bedrock stairs use weirdo_direction + upside_down_bit, NOT Java's 'facing'/'half'.

states.top_slot_bit: false=bottom slab, true=top slab (standard top/bottom placement)
states.minecraft:vertical_half: separate VERTICAL-slab orientation state (bottom|top) on newer vertical-slab variants — not the same as top_slot_bit

stone_block_slab.notes: stone_block_slab is the stone slab id family. Use top_slot_bit for bottom/top placement. Do NOT confuse with minecraft:vertical_half (vertical slabs). TODO: verify exact current slab states against Bedrock docs in the deferred Perplexity Run 3.

pink_stained_glass.notes: Color is part of the id in modern Bedrock, not a 'color' state.

pink_wool.notes: Color is part of the id (pink_wool), not a color data value, in modern Bedrock.

pink_concrete.notes: Solid hardened concrete. Color in id.

white_concrete.notes: Solid hardened concrete. Color in id.

sea_lantern.notes: Bright underwater-style light source, light level 15.

states.torch_facing_direction: unknown | west | east | north | south | top (Bedrock torch attachment side)

torch.notes: Bedrock torch uses torch_facing_direction (string enum). 'top' = standing on floor.

states.rail_direction: 0-5 (straight/ascending orientations; powered rail has no curved values 6-9)

golden_rail.notes: GOTCHA: Bedrock powered rail is golden_rail, NOT powered_rail. Uses rail_direction + rail_data_bit.

states.rail_direction: 0-9 (0-5 straight/ascending, 6-9 curved; regular rail supports curves)

rail.notes: Plain rail supports curved rail_direction values 6-9 unlike golden_rail.

oak_door.notes: Doors are two blocks: place lower then upper. upper_block_bit distinguishes the halves.

states.facing_direction: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 (north/south/west/east - the wall the ladder is attached to)

ladder.notes: Bedrock facing_direction integer enum (0=down,1=up,2=north,3=south,4=west,5=east). Ladder must attach to a wall (2-5).

pink_glazed_terracotta.notes: Glazed terracotta has a directional pattern; color is part of the id.
